title: Pasting Images
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I want to paste images in opencode. I [can see others do it with some success on other systems ](https://github.com/sst/opencode/issues/906#issue-3224845889) but I'm having some issues [on my stack](https://github.com/sst/opencode/issues/2878#issuecomment-3352442222). I'm not actually sure if this is a wezterm issue, wsl2 issue, or an opencode issue so if someone could point me in the right direction that woudl grealy be appreciated.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
To be able to paste images, specifically in opencode but in general as well?

And how do you copy the image exactly? From your file explorer? (so it already has a path)
Or from the web?

> If Opencode accesses the clipboard on its own via native tools, Wezterm isn't involved at all..

This is not exactly true. Wezterm has to deliver the signal to opencode. Stepping through Wezterm's code, it seems that Wezterm is _not_ delivering the signal if there's no text data in the clipboard. It seems to silently swallow the paste event if there is no text in the clipboard.
 
> OP mentions being on Windows through WSL2, I think this is an integration issue where OC doesn't know how to get the clipboard data from inside WSL2 🤔

I don't think this is true either. Opencode is WSL aware. [See here.](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/util/clipboard.ts#L47)

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I don't think this is accurate. I'm not a Rust nor Wezterm developer so please forgive me if I'm wrong about something here, but stepping through the code this is what I think is happening:

1. The entry point for the paste code is [here. ](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/main/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mod.rs#L2716-L2718)
2. `paste_from_clipboard` is implemented [here.](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/main/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mod.rs#L2716-L2718). Note how there's no pattern match for `Err`, only `Ok`.
3. The OS specific get_clipboard for Windows is raising an error. [We're calling `get_clipboard_string` here.](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/main/wezterm-gui/src/termwindow/mod.rs#L2716-L2718). The return type is also `Future<String>`.
4. If I keep following the call stack down you get to a call to Windows API `GetClipboardData(CF_UNICODETEXT)`. As I understand this will return NULL if there's only an image on the clipboard.

[Here's a gist with my full analysis.](https://gist.github.com/participant4/36db27cc0e4f2ce2261e72e29872d4bd)

It really seems that in Windows Wezterm silently swallows an error if there is no string on the clipboard. I may have that wrong, but I've done a bunch of digging to try and prove that theory wrong and come up empty.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Except that your first assumption is incorrect: `Ctrl-v` doesn't trigger `PasteFrom(source)` Take a look at the default Weztem keybindings: https://wezterm.org/config/default-keys.html The default key that triggers `PasteFrom(source)` is `Super-v` or `Ctrl-Shift-v`, NOT `Ctrl-v` which is normally sent to the terminal and that Opencode can detect freely like `Ctrl-u` for example. (note: `Super-v` is `Win-v` on Windows, but is usually never hit because Windows intercepts it itself for its clipboard history feature)

comments.body:
Thanks to this thread i was able to ask the correct question to ChatGPT. Im using Control+B to "paste" image.

```
-- wezterm.lua
local wezterm = require("wezterm")

local config = wezterm.config_builder()

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Window / startup
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
config.initial_cols = 120
config.initial_rows = 28

-- Pick your preferred default shell (uncomment one).
-- PowerShell 7 (pwsh) is usually nicer if installed:
-- config.default_prog = { "pwsh.exe", "-NoLogo" }
-- Windows PowerShell:
-- config.default_prog = { "powershell.exe", "-NoLogo" }

-- Ask before closing a window with running processes

-- Resize-only decorations (as you already do)
config.window_decorations = "RESIZE"

-- Add some breathing room around text
config.window_padding = { left = 10, right = 10, top = 8, bottom = 6 }

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Fonts / rendering
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
config.font = wezterm.font_with_fallback({
  { family = "JetBrains Mono", weight = "DemiBold" },
  { family = "Fira Code", weight = "Regular" },
  { family = "Segoe UI Emoji" }, -- emojis
})

config.font_size = 10
config.harfbuzz_features = { "calt=1", "liga=1", "clig=1" }

config.freetype_load_target = "Light"
config.freetype_render_target = "HorizontalLcd"

config.cursor_blink_rate = 650
config.default_cursor_style = "BlinkingBar"
config.force_reverse_video_cursor = true

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Colors / background
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
config.color_scheme = "AdventureTime"

config.window_background_image = "C:/Users/<user>/wizterm_wallpaper.png"
config.window_background_opacity = 0.90

config.window_background_image_hsb = {
  brightness = 0.15,
  hue = 1.0,
  saturation = 1.0,
}

config.inactive_pane_hsb = {
  saturation = 0.9,
  brightness = 0.7,
}

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Tabs / UI polish
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
config.enable_tab_bar = true
config.hide_tab_bar_if_only_one_tab = true
config.use_fancy_tab_bar = false
config.tab_max_width = 32
config.switch_to_last_active_tab_when_closing_tab = true

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scrollback / performance
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
config.scrollback_lines = 10000
config.adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size = false
config.animation_fps = 60
config.max_fps = 120

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Helpers: Clipboard image -> file -> paste path
-- ------------------------------------------------------------

---Return a temp directory path suitable for the current OS.
---@return string
local function get_temp_dir()
  -- Prefer OS temp env vars; fall back to HOME-based locations.
  local tmp = os.getenv("TMPDIR") or os.getenv("TEMP") or os.getenv("TMP")
  if tmp and #tmp > 0 then
    return tmp
  end

  if wezterm.target_triple == "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc" then
    -- Reasonable fallback on Windows if env vars are missing.
    local userprofile = os.getenv("USERPROFILE") or "C:\\"
    return userprofile .. "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp"
  end

  return "/tmp"
end

---Generate a fairly-unique filename (timestamp + random) with .png extension.
---@return string
local function make_random_png_name()
  -- Seed once per config load
  math.randomseed(os.time())
  local stamp = wezterm.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S") -- :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
  local r = math.random(100000, 999999)
  return ("wez_clip_%s_%d.png"):<nick>(stamp, r)
end

---Join directory + filename using OS-correct separator.
---@param dir string
---@param name string
---@return string
local function path_join(dir, name)
  if wezterm.target_triple == "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc" then
    -- Ensure we don't double up slashes
    dir = dir:gsub("[/]+$", "")
    return dir .. "\\" .. name
  end

  dir = dir:gsub("[/]+$", "")
  return dir .. "/" .. name
end

---Attempt to save clipboard image to outfile. Returns (ok:boolean, err:string|nil).
---@param outfile string
---@return boolean, string|nil
local function save_clipboard_image(outfile)
  -- WINDOWS: PowerShell + .NET Clipboard
  if wezterm.target_triple == "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc" then
    -- Use Windows PowerShell if present; otherwise pwsh should also work on Windows,
    -- but Clipboard types are most reliable in Windows PowerShell.
    local ps = "powershell.exe"

    -- PowerShell command:
    -- - Gets Clipboard image; if none, exits with non-zero.
    -- - Saves as PNG.
    -- - Prints the file path on success (not required, but helpful for debugging).
    local cmd = table.concat({
      "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop';",
      "Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms;",
      "Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing;",
      "$img=[System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard]::GetImage();",
      "if ($null -eq $img) { Write-Error 'Clipboard does not contain an image.' }",
      "$path='" .. outfile:gsub("'", "''") .. "';",
      "$img.Save($path,[System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png);",
      "Write-Output $path;",
    }, " ")

    local ok, stdout, stderr = wezterm.run_child_process({ ps, "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", cmd }) -- :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
    if not ok then
      return false, (stderr and #stderr > 0) and stderr or "Failed to run PowerShell to extract clipboard image."
    end
    return true, nil
  end

  -- macOS: pngpaste
  if wezterm.target_triple:find("apple") then
    -- pngpaste writes PNG from clipboard to file. It exits non-zero if no image.
    local ok, _, stderr = wezterm.run_child_process({ "pngpaste", outfile }) -- :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
    if not ok then
      return false, (stderr and #stderr > 0) and stderr or "pngpaste failed. Install with: brew install pngpaste"
    end
    return true, nil
  end

  -- Linux: try wl-paste (Wayland) then xclip (X11)
  -- Use bash -lc so we can do a small fallback script.
  local bash_script = table.concat({
    "set -euo pipefail;",
    "OUT=" .. wezterm.shell_quote_arg(outfile) .. ";",
    -- Wayland
    "if command -v wl-paste >/dev/null 2>&1; then",
    "  wl-paste --no-newline --type image/png > \"$OUT\" && exit 0;",
    "fi;",
    -- X11
    "if command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then",
    "  xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png -o > \"$OUT\" && exit 0;",
    "fi;",
    "echo 'No wl-paste or xclip found, or clipboard has no PNG image.' 1>&2;",
    "exit 2;",
  }, " ")

  local ok, _, stderr = wezterm.run_child_process({ "bash", "-lc", bash_script }) -- :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
  if not ok then
    return false, (stderr and #stderr > 0) and stderr or "Failed to extract clipboard image (need wl-paste or xclip)."
  end

  return true, nil
end

---Ctrl+b handler: save clipboard image to a random file and paste its path into the pane.
---@param window any
---@param pane any
local function paste_clipboard_image_path(window, pane)
  local tmpdir = get_temp_dir()
  local outfile = path_join(tmpdir, make_random_png_name())

  local ok, err = save_clipboard_image(outfile)
  if not ok then
    -- Show something actionable to you without breaking the session.
    wezterm.log_error("Clipboard image -> file failed: " .. (err or "unknown error"))
    -- Optional: also paste a comment into the terminal so you see it immediately.
    pane:send_paste("# wezterm: clipboard has no image (or missing deps)\n") -- :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
    return
  end

  -- Paste the full path directly into the active program.
  pane:send_paste(outfile) -- :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------
-- Keybindings
-- ------------------------------------------------------------
local act = wezterm.action

-- Better: use a leader key to create a “command mode”
config.leader = { key = "a", mods = "CTRL", timeout_milliseconds = 1000 }

config.keys = {
  -- Copy/Paste that match terminal muscle memory
  { key = "c", mods = "CTRL|SHIFT", action = act.CopyTo("Clipboard") },
  { key = "v", mods = "CTRL|SHIFT", action = act.PasteFrom("Clipboard") },

  -- NEW: Ctrl+b => save clipboard IMAGE to a file and paste the file path
  {
    key = "b",
    mods = "CTRL",
    action = wezterm.action_callback(function(window, pane) -- :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
      paste_clipboard_image_path(window, pane)
    end),
  },

  -- Quick font size adjust
  { key = "+", mods = "CTRL", action = act.IncreaseFontSize },
  { key = "-", mods = "CTRL", action = act.DecreaseFontSize },
  { key = "0", mods = "CTRL", action = act.ResetFontSize },

  -- Pane splits (tmux-like) using leader
  { key = "/", mods = "LEADER", action = act.SplitHorizontal({ domain = "CurrentPaneDomain" }) },
  { key = "-", mods = "LEADER", action = act.SplitVertical({ domain = "CurrentPaneDomain" }) },

  -- Move between panes (leader + hjkl)
  { key = "a", mods = "LEADER", action = act.ActivatePaneDirection("Left") },
  { key = "s", mods = "LEADER", action = act.ActivatePaneDirection("Down") },
  { key = "w", mods = "LEADER", action = act.ActivatePaneDirection("Up") },
  { key = "d", mods = "LEADER", action = act.ActivatePaneDirection("Right") },

  -- Toggle zoom for current pane
  { key = "z", mods = "LEADER", action = act.TogglePaneZoomState },

  -- Spawn a new tab in the same domain
  { key = "t", mods = "LEADER", action = act.SpawnTab("CurrentPaneDomain") },

  -- Keep your SHIFT+Enter behavior
  { key = "Enter", mods = "SHIFT", action = wezterm.action.SendString("\n") },

  -- Close current pane/tab with confirmation
  { key = "x", mods = "LEADER", action = act.CloseCurrentPane({ confirm = true }) },

  -- Search scrollback
  { key = "f", mods = "CTRL|SHIFT", action = act.Search("CurrentSelectionOrEmptyString") },
}

return config
```

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I've been working on a built-in solution for this and submitted a PR: #7621

It adds native clipboard image paste support across all platforms (macOS, Windows, Linux X11/Wayland) without requiring any Lua configuration or external tools (except `xclip`/`xsel` or `wl-paste` on Linux).

**How it works:**

- `Cmd+V` (macOS) / `Ctrl+V` (Windows/Linux) — smart paste: if the clipboard has text, paste text as usual; if it only has an image, save the image locally and paste the file path
- `PasteImageToSshUpload` — a new key assignment that uploads clipboard images to remote SSH servers via SFTP/SCP and pastes the remote path (useful for tools like Claude Code or OpenCode over SSH)
- Configurable via `image_paste_local_path` and `ssh_image_paste_remote_path`

This should address the core use case discussed here — pasting screenshots into CLI tools — natively, without needing per-user Lua workarounds.
